data.long_meaning: One who is skinny, weak or feeble. The name Qarni carries the meaning “Skinny” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Qarni usually hope their child will grow to embody skinny and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes resilience and determination in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Qarni belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Skinny.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qarni total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: قarni
in_arabic.meaning: من يتصف بالقرن أي العصر أو الزمان
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني الشخص الذي يعيش في عصر معين أو الزمن، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع مثل قوله تعالى: "وَلَقَدْ جَاءَ أَهْلُ الْفِيلِ مِنَ الْمُكَفِفِينَ وَمُتَكَسِفِينَ وَأَشْرَبَ النَّاسَ عَطَشَ الْقَرْنِ"، ويستخدم في العديد من الثقافات الإسلامية كدلالة على الانتماء لعصر أو فترة زمنية معينة.

in_urdu.name: قرنی
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو کسی خاص عہد یا زمانے میں رہتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: قرنی ایک مذکر اسم علم ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، اور اس کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو کسی خاص عہد یا زمانے میں رہتا ہے، جیسے کہ قرآن مجید میں کہا گیا ہے: "وَكُلُّهُم آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا"، اور یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں عہد یا دور کے ساتھ وابستہ ہونے کی علامت کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: क़रनी
in_hindi.meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो किसी विशेष युग या समय में रहता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: क़रनी एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, और इसका अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो किसी विशेष युग या समय में रहता है, जैसे कि कुरआन में कहा गया है: "और हर एक उनको क़यामत के दिन अकेले बुलाएगा", और यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में युग या काल के साथ जुड़ने के प्रतीक के रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है.

in_pashto.name: قرنی
in_pashto.meaning: هغه سړی چې په یو ځانګړي وخت یا پېړۍ کې ژوند کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: قرنی یو مذکر نوم دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، او معنی یې هغه سړی چې په یو ځانګړي وخت یا پېړۍ کې ژوند کوي، لکه څنګه چې قرآن کې ویل شوي دي: "او هر يو به يې د قيامت په ورځ يوازي راوبلل شي"، او دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې د وخت یا پېړۍ سره تړاو لرونکي په توګه کارول کېږي.

in_english.name: Qarni
in_english.meaning: One who lives in a particular era or time
in_english.long_meaning: Qarni is a masculine given name derived from Arabic roots, signifying an individual associated with a specific era or time period. Etymologically linked to the Arabic term 'qarn' (قَرن), meaning 'era' or 'generation', the name finds mention in the Quran in contexts referring to different epochs or generations. Historically, the name Qarni has been used across Islamic cultures to denote someone belonging to a particular age or period, symbolizing temporal identity and affiliation.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Qarni" has a symbolic representation in the Arabic language and culture, drawing from the physical trait of being skinny or weak. This name is often associated with attributes such as perseverance, determination and resilience, as those who carry this name may face challenges due to their physical condition yet continue to thrive. In an Islamic context, ones named Qarni may be recognized for their strong spirit and unwavering courage despite their physical limitations.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name "Qarni" has a deeper meaning, reminding us of the transient nature of our physical bodies and the importance of focusing on our spiritual growth. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The strong believer is better and dearer to Allah than the weak believer, though both are good." (Bukhari) Persisting through life's trials, even with a weak or frail body, demonstrates a strong faith and close relationship with Allah as Qarni individuals navigate their journey in this world, striving towards eternal paradise in the Hereafter.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya, Volume 11, page 83-84. The name Qarni carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: During the early days of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) mission in Mecca (610-622 AD).
historical_references.context: Qarni bin Hanzalah Al-Aslami was a polytheist poet from the tribe of Kindah who mocked the Meccan idols and ridiculed the Islamic Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Islam. He was known for his satirical poems against Islam and the Prophet. One day, prophet Muhammad (PBUH) visited the grave of his grandfather, Abdul-Muttalib, and found Qarni reciting poems near it. The Prophet (PBUH) addressed him and recited some verses from the Quran, which convinced Qarni to accept Islam.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tarikh Ibn Asakir, Volume 11, page 130. The name Qarni carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: After the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) migration to Medina (622 AD).
historical_references.context: Qarni bin Hanzalah Al-Aslami, who was a poet from the tribe of Kindah, had earlier embraced Islam during the Prophet's visit to his grandfather's grave in Mecca. However, he later relapsed into disbelief and began criticizing Islam publicly. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent Zaid ibn Arqam to confront him and invite him back to the fold of Islam. Eventually, Qarni was killed in the Battle of Hunain (630 AD) while fighting against the Muslim army.

modern_usage.modern_context: Qarni, in Islamic mythology, is a supernatural being also known as Al-Qarni, Al-Qarn, or Al-Qarneet. He is believed to live near the well of Zamzam in Mecca and is often depicted as a one-eyed, large-eared, and long-lived entity. In Islamic folklore, he is said to help those in need, answer questions, and grant requests. Qarni's story has gained popularity on various platforms, with Twitter users sharing stories and discussions about his legend; Reddit communities focusing on Islamic mythology and folklore frequently reference Qarni; and Wikipedia has an extensive entry about him, detailing his various attributes and appearances in different Islamic traditions.
